source.title: Highest rank of a polytope for A_n

task_boundary: Only source reading/cataloguing and mapping existing evidence. No new proof, mathematical computation, Lean, source acquisition, or admission.
source_principal_result: Theorem1.1 exact maximal ranks for all stated n; the new source contribution is the n≥12 upper bound, assembled from all maximal-parabolic branches.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Exact maximal string C-ranks: 0 at n=3,4,6,7,8; 3 at 5; 4 at 9; 5 at 10; 6 at 11; floor((n−1)/2) for every n≥12.
named_statements.qualification: The whole theorem is not recovered here. Lower existence and small degrees are borrowed by the source from [14] and [13], respectively.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Maróti alternative for primitive permutation groups: subset/product action, four Mathieu exceptions, or primitive order bound.
named_statements.qualification: Current accepted proof retains the exact original theorem, including the alternating-socle lower containment and subset-complement normalization; it does not rely on the abbreviated source formulation alone.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: A proper primitive subgroup of A_n with n≥12 and string C-rank d has d≤(n−3)/2.
named_statements.qualification: The source Table 1 exact maxima and its asymptotic aside are not inferred from this accepted finite-boundary proof.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: If some maximal parabolic of a string C-marking of A_n, n≥12, is primitive, then r≤(n−1)/2.
For primitive block degree m≠2, the block-image marking together with the omitted generator is connected and |R|≤1.
named_statements.qualification: Reusable block/commuting lemmas exist; the exact source application is not yet separately closed.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Transitive imprimitive parabolic with block size k>2 and block degree m>2 gives r≤floor((n−1)/2).
named_statements.qualification: Includes the source A_12 finite exclusion and the (4,4) action argument.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Literal arbitrary independent generating length of a primitive group of degree n≥8, other than A_n or S_n, is at most n−4.
named_statements.qualification: Literal statement is false: the already frozen five-generator degree-eight example has order 1344. The replacement bounds independent involutory strings, without IP. Root has communicated full mathematical/code/source review; no separate root-adoption file was present when this inventory was made.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Two-block transitive imprimitive maximal parabolic, with a transitive rank-two omission, gives r≤(n−1)/2.
named_statements.qualification: Current centralizer note supplies a supporting faithful-action reduction, not this whole branch; the source n=16 finite case remains.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Two-block transitive imprimitive maximal parabolic, all its rank-two omissions intransitive, gives r≤(n−1)/2.
An alternate full-graph path between endpoints of a selected eligible i-edge uses another i-edge.
Every selected cycle has zero or two edges of each colour; no multiple selected edges.
Two cycles sharing one selected i-edge share both; a selected square edge lies in no other simple cycle.
Every long selected cycle has adjacent edges with nonconsecutive labels.
A two-i-edge cycle permits replacing the selected i-edge by the missing one.
The same cycle also permits replacing the other selected i-edge.
Ordinary square slide changes two edges without increasing the square count.
Specific pictured middle-colour detour changes four edges.
named_statements.qualification: The current global middle-colour move replaces the literal local move; no automatic literal-claim equivalence is asserted.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: A paired selection can be chosen without a long cycle.
A paired selection can have only tree components or single-square unicyclic components.
Disconnected square-only selections reduce to three pictured nearest-square configurations.
If no connected paired selection exists, one can choose a tree component with all other components unicyclic.
named_statements.qualification: The accepted equality packet proves connectedness when 2r=n; the full source range of this proposition is not claimed.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: A full alternating square sharing a selected square edge has either both or neither of its other-colour edges selected.
named_statements.qualification: Connected-equality rigidity remains outstanding. The eight-point diagnostic only refutes an IP-free inference; it is not a counterexample to the source C-group statement.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: All full-graph edges meeting a selected square are selected, with a label adjacent to a square label.
When n≥9, selected-square vertices have degree at most three.
When n≥9, a square can be chosen with label difference two.
Both middle-colour edges meet the i−1,i+1 square in the pictured positions and have leaf endpoints.
For n≥9, a connected paired selection is a tree or the action embeds in C_2 wr S_(n/2).
Exact ladder actions: C_2×S_(n/2), or the full/even-base wreath group according to parity of n/2; continued on p22.
named_statements.qualification: Requires exact marked graph classification and group identification, not only a wreath embedding.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Primitivity of an orbit action forces its active label set to be an interval.
Maximal independent two-orbit block rank gives two consecutive labelled paths.
One-less-than-maximal block rank gives the two displayed graph patterns.
A residual generator moving more than one pair of M-orbits lowers the residual rank bound by one.
Block deficit one forces residual deficit at least one.
Maximal block rank forces residual deficit at least two.
If both orbit actions A and B are imprimitive, r≤(n−1)/2.
Two prescribed new double transpositions extend a transitive action to A_(n+4) or S_(n+4), according to parity.
named_statements.qualification: Explicitly quoted from [14], Proposition 3.3 or 5.4; not a new proof by this source or by this intake.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Sesqui-extension is isomorphic to the original group or its direct product with C_2; absence of the external involution preserves the C-property.
named_statements.qualification: Explicitly quoted from [14], Proposition 3.3 or 5.4; not a new proof by this source or by this intake.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: Primitive even connected C-markings of degree≤11 with all maximal parabolics intransitive are below the half-rank bound or among sixteen Table 2 diagrams.
named_statements.qualification: Full sixteen-diagram computational classification is a real proof input; it is not recovered by the separate primitive uniform-bound certificate.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: An extendible high-rank primitive prefix of degree<12 must be one of Table 2 diagrams (1)–(3), and dually.
Imprimitive action with all omissions intransitive satisfies the block-plus-orbit rank bound, the half-degree deficit, and exceptional parity/disconnection alternatives.
Smaller-degree even connected transitive C-markings with all omissions intransitive satisfy the induction bound, with equality forcing the alternating group.
A dihedral Table 2(1) orbit action gives the main bound when the exceptional three-generator end actions are excluded.
Interval orbit actions, not both alternating, give the main bound outside the specified exceptional ends.
Two alternating interval orbit actions give the main bound outside the specified exceptional ends.
Combines the interval-action cases for a non-end unique-crossing label.
No-gap path assertion from a nonsquare edge, plus an additional stated fixed-path conclusion.
named_statements.qualification: Accepted unique-crossing/no-gap version does not assert the extra fixed-path conclusion or silently exchange its prefix/tail conventions.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: For i=0, if the top generator acts on both maximal-parabolic orbits then r≤(n−1)/2.
named_statements.qualification: The already obtained note single_crossing_paths.tex is preserved unchanged; no new proof work was done for intake.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: For i=0, the last generator active on both orbits yields a support-deficit bound and an equality path graph.
named_statements.qualification: Literal statement puts X in the orbit fixed by the top generator; proof defines X as support of the tail. This wording requires explicit later reconciliation, not silent correction here.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: A transitive tail centralized nontrivially by an earlier generator has rank at most half its support minus one, with two equality ladder shapes.
A transitive prefix on the first orbit forces h=i+1 and a support deficit, with a specified equality graph.
An intransitive prefix on the first orbit yields the support deficit and a specified equality graph.
Combines the two prefix cases for i≠0 and an interval second orbit.
If i≠0 and the second orbit action is trivial, r≤(n−1)/2 for n≥8.
A transitive tail after the last shared generator gives the main bound or a specified exceptional small end action.
A sufficiently large fixed prefix and an intransitive tail with a paired selection give the main bound.
named_statements.qualification: Source explicitly reuses 4.10/4.12 without IP, diagram connectedness or evenness; the whole tail redistribution proof remains outstanding.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: A maximal unique-crossing label with shared later action reduces to an exceptional small tail or a trivial last-parabolic orbit.
For i=0 and trivial A, transitivity of the remaining tail outside the crossing pair gives the main bound.
The indicated small A action and transitivity of the tail on n−7 points give the main bound.
named_statements.qualification: The literal printed statement contains “F_x=∅” where its surrounding paragraph refers to Table 2(2)/(3). Recorded as an unresolved documentary discrepancy, not an accepted correction.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: For A trivial or a specified small action and B alternating, an intransitive tail with paired selection gives rank/support-deficit or explicit ladder alternatives.
named_statements.qualification: Includes all Tables 3–6 case exhaustions and their graph/group exclusion arguments.

named_statements.source_claim_summary: For A trivial or a specified Table 2 small action and B alternating, r≤(n−1)/2.

tables.scope: 15 listed primitive actions, source catalogue identifiers, and claimed exact maximal ranks.
tables.mapping: primitive accepts only the needed uniform bound; source group numbers are not silently converted to present GAP IDs.

tables.scope: Sixteen literal labelled permutation graphs used by 5.10–5.17 and the final exceptional-end branches.
tables.qualification: Actual graph labels, ordered markings, parity and all omission actions matter; group names/orders alone are insufficient.

tables.scope: Two A-trivial path patterns for |P|=n−2 and n−4.
A-trivial Q patterns (3),(4),(5a),(5b),(5c), seven displayed diagrams, for |Q|=n−2,n−3,n−4.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: String C-groups and regular abstract polytopes correspond, including the rank interpretation.
Prior exact small A_n ranks and all n≥12 lower-bound constructions complete the equality in Theorem1.1.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Retained [13]/[14] must be bound explicitly in any full recovery; not proved by our upper-bound components.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The earlier transitive non-S_n/non-A_n bound and high-rank S_n results are prerequisites.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Current L047 and earlier B results are reusable with whole common dependencies; no unpaid sibling premise.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Full marked action/IP definitions, one-edge and two-edge fracture selections, and the exhaustive primitive/imprimitive/all-intransitive partition.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Definitions read; the four-branch conclusion does not itself prove any branch.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Primitive ranks are asymptotically much less than n/2; alternative elementary order estimates might avoid classification at impractical finite cost.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: The asymptotic aside is not an output of the bounded constant-threshold proof. Babai/Pyber route is a suggestion, not an open problem solved here.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Maximal block system, independent block generators L, commuting set C and residual R; disconnected L has a special large-degree two-factor structure.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Supporting current L047 lemmas accepted; the complete L044 specialization is outstanding.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Magma exclusion of rank 6 or 7 polytopes for A12 in the k,m>2 branch.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Literal finite claim remains a required source application obligation; no new computation run.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The block-size-two split into block images S_m, A_m and other primitive groups, with permutation-module and centralizer arguments.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Some shared module and faithful centralizer lemmas accepted; exact whole branch, small m and all projected-independence claims remain.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The n=16 two-large-block finite exclusion within the transitive double-omission branch.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Not inferred from the separately accepted L047 ten-action lemma without an explicit reduction.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Two earlier fracture facts quoted from [15], Propositions3.2 and3.6.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Retained source references; orbit-cut versions exist but exact use must be routed.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The paired-selection branch for A_n ends by either an edge deficit or exclusion of the precise ladder groups.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Not complete until connected rigidity and exact C4.19 group identifications are supplied.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Unique eligible crossing yields exactly two maximal-parabolic orbits and the three-case interval/imprimitive decomposition.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Endpoint fact accepted in paired_cuts; complete subsequent case partition/proofs remain.
Retained [13]/[14]; ordered markings and whether the external involution belongs to the extension must be preserved.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The source explicitly claims its 4.10/4.12 tools do not need IP, diagram connectedness, or evenness.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Normal form and equality consequence are accepted with that limited scope; later rigidity is not thereby accepted IP-free.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: The Tables3–6 graphs exhaust the last support-deficit cases; certain pictured alternatives produce improper intersections or odd generators.
unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.current_disposition: Main proof obligations, not disposable ancillary data.

unnumbered_principal_and_dependency_clai.claim: Final two-ended support gluing uses X∪Y=Ω and the overlap-rank bound; the four source branches exhaust all cases.
